title: Going to New York in 1936 and meeting the Pollack band
summary: Sharkey explains how he went to New York after the Chapery, with Frank Federico and Ray Bonitas, and met Ben Pollack's band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, you said something about being in New York, the first...like since 1939. I remember that's the first New Orleans band I really heard in person. That was 1936 when you were up at Nick's. Remember down there? You go down a few steps to the old Nick's on 7th Avenue.

That's right. It was in 1939. It was...when I went to New York, it was 1936. When I went to work for Nick, it was going into 1937. Yeah. In other words, this is how I got to New York. I just finished a place called the Chapery. It's right out here in West End. It's now the Maison Restaurant. Oh yeah. This was the Chapery. It was run by Joe Loicana, Steve Loicana, and Angelo Gemelli. They had a nightclub. And it was a pretty big place. Yeah. And at that time, they had a woman by the name of Ming Toy. She was a striptease. In other words, she didn't dance or take her clothes off. She used to dance like Sally Rand with the fans. Oh yeah. And it'd become a big hit here. So I played there for about a year or so, and left there, and I wasn't doing anything at all. And I don't know if you know this man, his name is Ray Bonitas, he plays a wonderful bass. But I know you know Frank Frederica. Oh yes. Oh yeah. So Wingy Menor is in New York, and he sends for Frank Frederica and Ray Bonitas to come up to New York. He had a job waiting for them. And Ray Bonitas and Frank are very good friends of mine. So they said, come take a ride to New York with us. And I said, well what am I going to do in New York? I don't have no job. You fellas have a job. They said, come on. This Ray Bonitas, he's always had a lot of money. His people had a lot of money. So they said, don't worry about anything. Just come on. If you feel like you want to go back home, I'll just give you the money and you can go back home. So we got to New York, and we were there about a week. And Ben Pollack came to New York. Now you know Ben Pollack. And they had a fine band. And in other words he had Farzola.
Is Harry James one of those names?
Harry James. He had the trombone player. He was in the Army and got lost in the plane. Glenn Miller he had. Ray Badu. Eddie Miller. Snappy Lamar. He had all of them.
Oh yeah, that old band he had with Benny Goodman and other.
Benny was in the band a little earlier before that I guess.
